title: Blobby's Woodland Wonder
desc: A mobile game that connects animal-matching puzzles, stack sorting, village building, and exploration in one woodland world.
alt: Blobby's Woodland Wonder game artwork published on ListPull
synopsis: Blobby's Woodland Wonder is one of the mobile products I work on through ListPull. The challenge is bringing several puzzle mechanics into one game without making it feel like a collection of unrelated screens. Animal matching, stack sorting, village building, and exploration all behave differently, but the player still needs to understand how they fit together. That takes consistent menus, clear feedback, and a lot of attention to what happens when someone taps, moves, or finishes a level. My role as founder covers product direction and engineering, alongside the wider creative work that goes into the game. I include it because mobile development calls for a different kind of thinking from a business dashboard or cloud service. There is still application state to manage and features to connect, but timing, movement, and the feel of the experience matter just as much.

title: Creative Editing Applications
kind: Creative software · Image and vector editing
desc: Image and vector editing work focused on layered artwork, object transforms, reusable design controls, and reliable import and export workflows.
alt: Blobby promotional artwork published by ListPull, an example of the company's digital artwork
credit: Real ListPull artwork · not an editor screenshot
synopsis: Creative software has been part of my work since I automated artwork production in Adobe Illustrator and Photoshop. At ListPull, that experience carries into applications for working with images and vector graphics. The problem is not just putting a drawing surface on the screen. Someone might import artwork, move an object, change its layer, adjust a shape, undo a mistake, and export the result. Each step needs to agree about what changed. The engineering work is in representing the artwork, keeping selections and properties in sync, and making sure edits do not disappear when someone switches tools. It also means designing controls that are precise without slowing people down. This project brings together the creative work I started with and the application development I've done since. It's an example of solving a production problem with software, not just making a screen that looks like an editor.

title: Video Editing & Production
desc: Video production software that brings footage, layered timelines, titles, audio, previews, and export tasks into a connected editing workflow.
alt: Wildlife-themed media artwork published on the ListPull website
credit: Real ListPull media artwork · not an editor screenshot
synopsis: Editing video is a good example of why an application's behavior matters as much as how it looks. A production workflow has to keep footage, clips, timing, titles, audio, and exports organized. A change to one clip affects what appears at a particular point in the timeline, sometimes alongside several other tracks. The engineering challenge is keeping those pieces in sync while someone makes changes and checks the result. At ListPull, media production also connects with our wildlife publishing and creative projects, so the editing work is tied to the practical needs of making and preparing content. This project shows my work around interactive controls, media handling, previews, and the details that make a complicated workspace manageable. There is a lot going on behind a simple trim or title adjustment. The goal is to keep that complexity out of the person's way.

title: AI Research & Development Workflows
kind: AI applications · Data retrieval and code workflows
desc: Natural-language research and development workflows connecting data sources, PostgreSQL, APIs, AI models, and usable results.
role: Founder / AI and full-stack engineering · ListPull
alt: Illustration of a code editor, live app preview, and optional AI chat panel
synopsis: One of the applications I've worked on at ListPull handles research questions over structured data. The problem was the back-and-forth between asking a question, finding the right records, and turning those records into a useful answer. The work combined Ollama, PostgreSQL, third-party API retrieval, and responses that could be streamed as the analysis was prepared. That's a different problem from adding a chat window to a page. The request has to connect to real information, the right data needs to be retrieved, and the result needs enough context to make sense. My background also includes AI integration and building full-stack applications, so I look at how these features fit into a working system. The related code and AI workspace demonstrates some of the interaction patterns, while the larger work includes the data access and services behind them.

title: Market Analytics & Data Platforms
desc: A market analytics platform bringing multiple data feeds together through APIs, backend services, authenticated views, and time-series charts.
role: Founder / full-stack and data engineering · ListPull
alt: Illustration of the Business Insights data explorer with charts and sample data
synopsis: Market data gets complicated when it comes from different providers. Each feed can have its own format, update schedule, missing values, and limits. I worked on a ListPull analytics platform that brings those sources into a common research interface. The engineering involved React and Angular views, PHP services, WordPress-backed authentication, external API integrations, and time-series charts. The hard part wasn't drawing a graph. It was collecting, organizing, and serving the information so the graph had something useful behind it. That also meant thinking through what happens when a provider is slow or its data changes. My work connected the front end to the services and data feeding it. I include this project because it shows the full-stack side of analytics, from getting information into the system to making it readable on screen. A CSV example shows only a small part of that work.

title: Forecasting Services
desc: Node.js forecasting services using ARIMA models, per-symbol caching, data-provider integrations, and intraday and daily projections.
alt: Illustration of Forecast Lab with a line chart showing past data and a projected trend
credit: Illustration of the live tool, example values
synopsis: Forecasting is useful when it is part of a working data pipeline, not just a line added to a chart. I built forecasting services for ListPull using Node.js and ARIMA models, with per-symbol caching and intraday and daily projections. That work sits on top of data retrieval and time-series handling. The service needs to keep observations tied to the right symbol, avoid repeating expensive model work when it can reuse a result, and return estimates without treating them like measured facts. The interface has its own job: show where the real observations stop and where the projection starts. I include this work because it connects backend services, statistical models, provider integrations, and clear data presentation. It also involves practical limits, like incomplete data and rate limits from outside services. The small forecasting example on ListPull shows the idea, not the full service behind it.

title: Wildlife Media & Publishing
desc: A cross-platform wildlife media project connecting photography, short-form video, website presentation, and content publishing.
role: Founder / media and platform direction · ListPull
alt: Wildlife photography featured on ListPull's website
synopsis: ListPull's wildlife work brings together animal photography, short videos, and stories shared through its website and social channels. The project is about more than making individual pieces of media. Content needs to be organized, sized for different screens, presented consistently, and connected so people can find related work. My role is in the company's product and platform direction, not a claim that I photographed every animal or edited every clip. This work draws on my background in digital media and on the software side of publishing: page layouts, navigation, media handling, and keeping a recognizable presentation across different places. It also overlaps with Blobby and ListPull's creative applications. I include it because not every technical project is an enterprise dashboard. Building a good experience around pictures and video still involves product choices, engineering decisions, and plenty of details that people notice when they don't work.

title: Clinic Recommendations
kind: Enterprise application · AI and cloud architecture
desc: An AI-assisted clinic recommendation feature built into a React application, backed by AWS workflows, PostgreSQL, Bedrock, and OpenSearch.
alt: Simplified diagram of the clinical recommendation pipeline, not a client screen
synopsis: At Accenture, I led engineering work on a clinic recommendation feature for Bristol Myers Squibb. The feature was added to an existing React application and used lab information to help surface relevant clinic options. On the back end, the work involved AWS Step Functions, Lambda, PostgreSQL, Bedrock embeddings, and OpenSearch. My role included helping the team connect these pieces and make the result usable in the application people already had. What I took away from this project is that AI features don't live on their own. They still need dependable data, clear rules, careful testing, and an interface that makes sense to the person using it. This was also sensitive work, so the portfolio doesn't show private data or a real client screen. The diagram is a simplified view of how the systems fit together, not a copy of the production setup.

title: Public Health Systems
desc: Connected Salesforce contact-center operations with AWS services to support call routing, digital vaccination records, and public-health follow-up work.
role: Application architect and senior engineer · Accenture
alt: Simplified diagram of public health system integrations, not a client screen
synopsis: At Accenture, I worked on public health systems that had to pass information between different tools and teams. One part of the work connected Salesforce contact center operations with AWS Connect, so calls and follow-up steps could move through a more organized process. I also worked on digital vaccination record access and disease tracking workflows. These projects taught me how much time can be lost when people have to repeat a step or copy information from one system to another. The technical work included APIs, cloud services, routing rules, and data handling, but the reason for building them was practical: make the work easier for the people doing it. I worked as a senior engineer and later in an architecture leadership role. The image is a general diagram, not a government system or an actual patient record.

title: Bureau of Labor Statistics Website
desc: Modernized public statistical reports with reusable React components, Highcharts visualizations, government APIs, and automated publishing tools.
alt: Illustration of a public data dashboard, not an official BLS screenshot
synopsis: At BAE Systems, I helped modernize the public Bureau of Labor Statistics website for the U.S. Department of Labor. I worked on reusable React components, charts built with Highcharts, and pages that pulled in government data through APIs. I also wrote tests and helped with publishing tools for articles, images, and PDFs. This kind of work isn't flashy, but it matters. People visit public data websites because they need to find a number, understand a chart, or check something they heard. If the page is hard to use or the data is presented poorly, the information isn't doing its job. I learned a lot about accessibility, careful testing, and keeping a large website consistent while different teams work on it. The image here is an illustration, not an official BLS screenshot. You can follow the link to the public site.
